children: Kumar will succeed Sanjeeb Chaudhuri from May 10, 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, while Pradeep Natarajan has been reappointed for another three-year term

IDFC First Bank has approved the appointment of S Ganesh Kumar as its part-time non-executive chairperson and the reappointment of Pradeep Natarajan as executive director for a further three years. The bank announced the board-level changes on October 24, following recommendations from its Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

Kumar, currently an independent director on the bank’s board, will succeed Sanjeeb Chaudhuri, whose tenure as part-time non-executive chairperson is scheduled to end on May 9, 2027. Kumar’s appointment will take effect on May 10, 2027, and continue until April 29, 2029, subject to approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and other requisite regulatory clearances.

The board has also approved Natarajan’s reappointment as whole-time director, designated executive director, for a three-year term beginning June 1, 2027, and ending May 31, 2030. His current term expires on May 31, 2027. The reappointment is subject to RBI approval and other applicable clearances.

Separately, independent director Aashish Kamat will leave the board at the close of business on December 17, 2026, upon completing his second term and reaching the maximum tenure permitted under the applicable banking regulations.
S Ganesh Kumar Brings Over Three Decades Of RBI Experience

Kumar previously served as an executive director at the RBI, where he spent more than three decades. His responsibilities included payment and settlement systems, strategic planning, external investments and the management of foreign exchange reserves.

He was associated with the Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology and contributed to the establishment of institutions such as the National Payments Corporation of India, RBI Information Technology Private Limited and Indian Financial Technology and Allied Services.

Kumar also worked with the National Cyber Security Council and was associated with the framing of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act. His contributions included the conceptualisation and development of technology-led retail payment systems in India.
His experience spans central banking, financial infrastructure, digital payments and technology-led initiatives in the financial services sector.
Pradeep Natarajan To Continue Leading Retail Banking

Natarajan has held leadership positions at IDFC FIRST Bank since December 2018 and currently heads its retail banking business. His areas of expertise include business development, technology, risk analytics, debt management, project management, customer service and marketing.
Before joining IDFC FIRST Bank, he held leadership roles at Standard Chartered Bank, Dell India, Religare Macquarie Wealth Management and Capital First.

The appointments form part of the bank’s board-level decisions aimed at ensuring continuity in its leadership structure. Both Kumar’s appointment and Natarajan’s reappointment remain subject to the required regulatory approvals.
